text: CJP president Abhijeet Dipke posted an Instagram note explaining his earlier criticism of singer Diljit Dosanjh and urging him to end the dispute. Diljit responded on stage at his Delhi concert, saying he supports the protesters but asks not to be taught how to fight, Hindustan Times reports.

sources.title: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke explains why he criticised Diljit Dosanjh after singer's fiery response, wants 'older brother' to end row | Hindustan Times - Hindustan Times
sources.articleText:
After singer Diljit Dosanjh lashed out at the Cockroach Janata Party from the stage at his Delhi concert on Friday, CJP president Abhijeet Dipke responded to the singer, offering to end the row. Dipke had criticised Diljit for his apparent silence and evasive answer during the students' protests in June. Diljit addressed those remarks on Friday in a rather curt tone.
On Friday, while performing at his concert in Delhi, Diljit addressed the crowd about the criticism he received for saying “I’m just an artist,” when asked to comment on the students' protests back in June. Without naming the CJP directly, the singer said, “I love all of you because I am an artist, bro. I am being quiet, so let me stay quiet. I support all of you. But don't teach Punjabis how to fight.” He then addressed the remarks about Satluj and chided those who made fun of it on stage.
Later on Friday night, Abhijeet Dipke took to Instagram to share a note for the singer. Explaining why he criticised him, Dipke wrote, “Paaji, back in June, when we were protesting, I was a little hurt by your comment. Not because I had anything against you personally, but because I've always seen you as someone who speaks up for the cause, just like you said yourself.”
In his post, the CJP founder also shared a picture of himself at Diljit’s concert earlier this year and said he had always been an admirer. “If anything, I've always been an admirer of yours, and that hasn't changed. I still listen to your music. In fact, I came to your concert in Chicago this May, just before returning to India, not just for your music, but because I've always had immense respect for the person you are. Your courage, your authenticity, and the way you've taken India to the global stage while staying so true to your roots are things I've always admired about you. And I guess that's why the comment hurt a little, because I've always held you in such high regard. But one disagreement or misunderstanding doesn't change the respect and admiration I have for you,” he added.
Addressing himself as Diljit’s ‘younger brother’, Dipke added, “Baaki paaji, chhota bhai samajh ke mitti pao (Consider me your younger brother and end this matter).” He then wrote a line from Diljit’s song GOAT about being cordial with both enemies and friends. “And at last I would just like to say, "Gabru ta vairi nu vi mitha bolda, ni tu ta ferr jatt da pyar goriye.”
Meanwhile, Diljit Dosanjh kicked off his RuPay AURA India Tour 2026 with a sold-out show at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in the national capital on Friday. The tour is the India leg of the singer's globally popular Aura Tour.
Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Film Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera).
